_about: Percent of measured manual wheelchair users who could reach a 4 x 4 in (100 x 100 mm) spot, by height from the floor and horizontal distance from the chair. Copied cell by cell from the two charts.
source: D'Souza C, Steinfeld E, Paquet V (IDeA Center, University at Buffalo), Feathers D (Cornell). Design Resource #20: Functional Reach Capability for Wheeled Mobility Users. Updated Jan 4, 2011. Figures 1 and 2. Funded by the U.S. Access Board (TDP-02-C-0033) and NIDRR (H133E990005). https://idea.ap.buffalo.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/110/2019/08/20.pdf
task: Placing an empty 2 oz (56 g) canister on a shelf; not a pushing, gripping or precision task.
_measured_note: Only the 235 of 276 manual wheelchair users who could grasp and reach above shoulder height were measured, so the chart percentages are of those 235. Multiplying by 235/276 gives the share of everyone recruited, counting the 41 who were left out as unable to reach (the cautious reading).
_good_design_note: The charts' own colour key: 75-100% Good Design, 50-74% Fair, 25-49% Poor, 0-24% Very Bad.
_lowest_note: Data for some or all participants was not collected below points considered unsafe to attempt reaching; the 300-399 mm row is not a measurement of ability. Their key finding 4: many could not safely reach the ADA 15 in (380 mm) low limit, and they recommend 28 in (700 mm).

forward._reference: Horizontal distance from the forward-most point of the person or chair (footrests). Positive = reaching out past it, e.g. over a counter; negative = target closer, possible only with knee/toe space underneath.

side._reference: Horizontal distance from the side-most point of the person or chair. Positive = reaching out past it.

chair_edge_to_wall_m._note: Where the chair sits for each approach, matching body.json: forward = footrests at the wall; side = side of the chair about 0.1 m from the wall. Estimate (interpolated).
